summary: Quarterly renewal/check-in. Greenleaf is evaluating a capacity upgrade (+2 GPUs), adding EU region for low-latency inference, and a 12-month contract extension. Key blockers: latency validation in EU, security attestation (SOC2/KMS), and budget approval timing. Agreed next steps include benchmarks, contract amendment, and security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Redwood CSM), Carla Ruiz (Greenleaf Head of AI), Marcus Lee (Platform Eng), Nadia Hassan (Security), Tom Brooks (Procurement)

Summary: quick touch to confirm renewal interest and scope for expansion to EU region and additional capacity. Lots of back-and-forth on benchmarks and security docs.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick agenda - renewals, capacity, EU region, security questions, and next steps. Carla, you wanted to lead with any updates on your side?
00:18 Speaker 2 (Carla): Yeah thanks, Maya. Overall we're happy with Redwood - latency has been pretty solid in us-east - but we are seeing increased load ahead of the holiday vertical and want to add two more GPU slots for our cart recommendation model. Also we have a compliance push in EU so need an eu region ability, ideally managed by Redwood but with VPC peering.
00:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great, that's helpful. Marcus, do you have the traffic numbers you shared in the renewal sheet?
00:48 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Yep, 95th p90 latencies are fine in us-east now but we expect 2.5x Q4 increase. We would like to reserve capacity to keep p95 under 250ms for the small model. Current infra is 4x A10 equivalent, asking +2 GPUs - pref on dedicated.
01:12 Speaker 2 (Liam): Quick clarification - when you say dedicated, do you mean Dedicated pools in Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity or private on-prem?
01:20 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Reserved capacity on Dedicated. We want the SLAs and isolation but still using Redwood managed control plane.
01:28 Speaker 1 (Maya): Got it. For EU region, we support eu-west-1 today, we can do dedicated capacity there but we'd need to validate throughput under your workload. That means a quick benchmark run. Are you ok with Redwood running an end-to-end sim against your sample traces?
01:42 Speaker 4 (Carla): Yes - we'll share sanitized traces. Main thing is SLOs - p95 sub-300ms is our target in EU.
01:52 Speaker 5 (Nadia): On security, top asks: SOC 2 Type II, customer-managed KMS or HSM options, SSO/SAML integration, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also need network diagrams for VPC peering.
02:10 Speaker 2 (Liam): Totally - we have SOC2, we can send that. KMS integrations supported, we have HSM partners for private if needed. For audit logs we can forward via secure syslog or cloud export. I'll compile the network diagram and KMS notes.
02:28 Speaker 6 (Tom): Procurement timeline - if we sign amendment by mid-June we can lock pricing for Q3-Q4 spend. Budget cycles close end of June.
02:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): So a reasonable plan - we send updated pricing and contract amendment this week, run the EU benchmark next week, and if it meets p95 target, lock in extension and capacity. Any deal breakers?
02:53 Speaker 4 (Carla): Pricing is the main thing - also need to know if dedicated capacity can burst cross-region during peak.
03:02 Speaker 2 (Liam): We have burst policies; we can outline cost for burst traffic. Also possible to route to compatible model variants to reduce cost during spikes.
03:12 Speaker 3 (Marcus): One technical question - is KV cache and prefix caching preserved when we move to EU dedicated pools? We rely on cold-start mitigation for cart recs.
03:24 Speaker 2 (Liam): Good call - the caching design keeps KV cache warm per pool; cross-region cache isn't shared by default. We can discuss replication or warm-up strategies for the canary start. For immediate term, we can preload key prefixes as part of the benchmark.
03:42 Speaker 4 (Carla): Ok that helps. On security again - can you confirm data retention for logs and ability to set retention policies from the console?
03:53 Speaker 2 (Liam): Yes, Audit log retention configurable; enterprise plans can set custom retention and export. We'll include screenshots in the docs.
04:05 Speaker 6 (Tom): Contract specifics - we want a 12-month extension with commitment to the additional 2 GPUs and an option to renew for another 12 months at pre-agreed uplift. Can you draft an amendment?
04:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): Absolutely, I'll prepare the contract amendment and capacity table. We'll price the EU dedicated pool and the +2 GPUs.
04:28 Speaker 5 (Nadia): One more - encryption at rest and in transit, full key rotation policy, and attestations for third-party sub processors.
04:40 Speaker 2 (Liam): We support TLS, AES-256 at rest, and integrate with customer KMS. We'll include the key rotation schedule and list of subprocessors in the security packet.
04:50 Speaker 4 (Carla): Great. For the benchmark, our SLOs: p95 < 300ms, 99th < 600ms, and cost per 1k requests target. We'll share exact numbers.
05:03 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Also need notes on model quantization differences - we're using a quantized variant in production and want to ensure parity.
05:12 Speaker 2 (Liam): We'll run the same quantized artifact - if there are discrepancies we'll flag where kernel scheduling or compilation may differ. We can run both float32 and q4 benchmarks.
05:24 Speaker 1 (Maya): To recap: Redwood will send amendment and price by Friday 2026-05-22, Liam will run EU benchmark using your sanitized traces week of 2026-05-25, Marcus will provide traffic profile by 2026-05-24, Nadia will review security docs by 2026-05-28, and Tom will aim to move procurement if benchmarks and docs look good.
05:43 Speaker 4 (Carla): Sounds good. A couple of smaller items - can we add per-route dashboards to show token-level cost for cart recs? That helps our FinOps team.
05:55 Speaker 2 (Liam): Yes, per-route analytics are available - we can enable route-level dashboards and share a sample dashboard link.
06:05 Speaker 6 (Tom): On pricing, any discounts for committing to 12 months and +2 capacity?
06:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes - we'll include tiered discounts for annual commitments and for committed capacity. I'll model a few scenarios in the amendment.
06:20 Speaker 3 (Marcus): One risk to call out - if eu warm-up causes transient errors, will Redwood provide a fallback to us-east automatically? We don't want customer-facing errors.
06:32 Speaker 2 (Liam): We can configure smart routing and automatic fallbacks to a compatible model in us-east. We'll document failover latency and routing policies.
06:45 Speaker 4 (Carla): Great. Any open questions from Redwood?
06:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): None, just making sure we have owners and dates. We'll email the amendment and schedule the benchmark.
06:56 Speaker 5 (Nadia): Quick clarification: for KMS, do you support bringing our own key in HSM via your private deployment or is it limited to hosted with customer-managed KMS?
07:08 Speaker 2 (Liam): Both paths possible: hosted with customer-managed KMS is simplest; private/VPC with dedicated HSM is available for enterprise. We'll include options and cost deltas.
07:22 Speaker 4 (Carla): Okay, thanks everyone. If benchmarks hit targets we aim to sign by 2026-06-10 to ensure provisioning in July.
07:34 Speaker 1 (Maya): Perfect. Thanks all. We'll follow up with the docs and benchmark schedule.

(end of recording)

Notes: transcription contains small mis-hearings (names sometimes transcribed), timestamps are rough every 15-90 seconds. References: "amendment" (contract), "Dedicated" (Redwood Dedicated product), "KV cache", "VPC peering", "KMS/HSM", "SOC2".
